source: Kaelbling, Littman, Cassandra (1998) Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains
finding: A POMDP reduces to a fully observable MDP over belief states. Optimal finite-horizon value is piecewise linear and convex in the belief, as a max over policy trees.
numbers: Tiger problem: open correct door +10, wrong door -100, listen -1. Optimal infinite-horizon rule: keep listening until the tiger was heard twice more on one side than the other.
quote: keep listening until you have heard the tiger twice more on one side than the other
limits: Exact solution needs enumeration of policy trees. No known a priori bound on optimal plan graph size.
agent_relevance: Belief plus a stop rule is a clean template for our S0 gate: gather evidence until a count threshold is reached, then commit.

source: Kaelbling, Littman, Cassandra (1998) Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains
finding: Optimal memory need is fragile. Lowering listen accuracy from 0.85 to 0.65 makes the optimal plan graph much larger.
numbers: Listen reliability 0.85 -> 0.65: plan graph grows from a few nodes to a much larger graph (Fig 16 vs Fig 18).
limits: Single toy problem. Shows sensitivity, not a general law.
agent_relevance: Noisy observations demand more state kept in the scaffold. Do not assume a fixed short notes budget works for noisier evidence.

source: Silver, Veness (2010) Monte-Carlo Planning in Large POMDPs (POMCP)
finding: Particle-filter belief plus tree search over histories scales online POMDP planning to about 1e18 (battleship) and 1e56 (pocman) states, needing only a black-box simulator.
numbers: Rocksample (11,11), 247,808 states: POMCP 20.01 +/-0.23 vs SARSOP 21.56 +/-0.11 (SARSOP used ~1000 s offline, POMCP 1 s per action). Rocksample (15,15), 7.37M states: POMCP 15.32, rollout 7.56. Rocksample (7,8): POMCP 20.71 vs HSVI-BFS 21.46.
limits: Needs a good simulator and prior knowledge for rollouts. In battleship the search tree gave only a small gain over rollouts because action values differ little and returns are noisy.
agent_relevance: Sampling hypotheses (particles) about the hidden state and simulating forward is a usable pattern for an LLM that has a world model but not explicit probabilities.

source: Silver, Veness (2010) POMCP
finding: Domain knowledge (preferred actions) cut required search. Battleship: POMCP sank all ships over 50 moves faster than random play and over 25 moves faster than random choice among preferred actions.
numbers: Battleship 10x10, 5 ships; reward -1 per step, +100 on finish; ~1e18 states.
limits: Gain from preferred actions shrinks as simulations per move grow.
agent_relevance: Cheap action pruning priors help most under small budgets. Matches budget-aware design.

source: Hausknecht, Stone (2015) Deep Recurrent Q-Learning for POMDPs
finding: Adding an LSTM lets a one-frame agent handle flickering screens, but gives no systematic benefit over stacking frames on standard games.
numbers: Flickering Pong (screens obscured with p=0.5): DRQN with 1 frame integrates information. Across ten flickering games, no systematic gain from recurrence. Across 9 standard Atari games DRQN roughly equals DQN (better on Frostbite and Double Dunk, worse on Beam Rider). Trained on full games, DRQN degrades more gracefully when tested on flickering.
quote: recurrency confers no systematic benefit compared to stacking the observations in the input layer
limits: Pong is an outlier. Only 9 games, one architecture, early DQN training protocol.
agent_relevance: Memory in the loop is not free value. Test whether a belief-tracking step helps on the actual task before adding it.

source: Ni, Eysenbach, Salakhutdinov (2022) Recurrent Model-Free RL Can Be a Strong Baseline for Many POMDPs
finding: Re-tuned plain recurrent model-free RL matches or beats 6 specialized POMDP methods. Earlier reports of its weakness were largely implementation effects.
numbers: Better sample efficiency and asymptote on 18 of 21 environments. Beats VRM on 6 of 8 occlusion tasks. Worse on Ant-Dir and Humanoid-Dir vs on-policy variBAD. Oracle with hidden state sometimes did worse than the recurrent agent (same untuned hyperparameters). 5x faster, 200x less RAM than VRM, but 17.5x slower wall-clock than MRPO.
limits: Authors note the oracle result likely reflects untuned oracle hyperparameters. Benchmarks are continuous control, not language.
agent_relevance: Strong baseline warning: before crediting a belief or planning module, compare to a well-tuned plain memory baseline.

source: Ni et al. (2022) Recurrent Model-Free RL
finding: Ablations show what moves performance: algorithm choice and context length are task-dependent; inputs must let the agent infer the hidden state.
numbers: Adding past rewards to inputs: Walker-P 981.6 -> 1345.0 (1.3x). TD3 -> SAC on Ant-P: 310.7 -> 2123.5 (6.8x). Context length 64 -> 5 on Walker-V: 2.2x; 64 -> 400 on Cheetah-Vel: 0.292 -> 0.415 (1.4x). LSTM vs GRU: no significant general difference.
limits: Best context length is problem-specific and needs tuning.
agent_relevance: Reward and feedback history are part of the belief state. Keep prior outcomes visible in the scaffold context.

source: Henderson et al. (2018) Deep Reinforcement Learning that Matters
finding: Seed variance alone can make identical RL setups look statistically different. Small-N reports are unreliable.
numbers: TRPO on HalfCheetah, same hyperparameters, two sets of 5 seeds: t = -9.0916, p = 0.0016. Another comparison: t = 1.03, p = 0.334 (not different). Five trials per config in their experiments.
limits: Policy-gradient continuous control only; about reproducibility in general, not POMDP results specifically.
agent_relevance: Our agent evaluations need many seeds and paired tests. Single runs of an agent loop prove little.

source: Krishnamurthy et al. (2024) Can Large Language Models Explore In-Context?
finding: LLMs do not explore reliably in bandits without help. Only one of 32 prompt designs on GPT-4 worked: suggestive hint, externally summarized history, chain of thought, temperature 0.
numbers: K=5 arms, gap 0.2, T=100. Basic GPT-4 prompt: suffix failure (never picks best arm in the second half) in over 60% of replicates. Winning config BSSC0: SuffFailFreq(T/2)=0.00, median reward 0.47 (TS 0.47, UCB 0.55). Raw-history CoT fails.
quote: externally summarized interaction history, presented as sufficient statistics
limits: Simple stateless bandit. Needs external summarization into sufficient statistics, which may be unavailable in complex tasks. GPT-3.5 and Llama2 failed in all configs.
agent_relevance: Strong support for scaffold-side belief summaries: the harness should compute counts, means and posterior summaries and feed them, not rely on the model reading raw history.

source: Qiu et al. (2025) Bayesian Teaching Enables Probabilistic Reasoning in LLMs
finding: Off-the-shelf LLMs barely update beliefs across five interaction rounds of a flight-preference task. Chain of thought, numeric formats, 30 rounds and base models did not fix it.
numbers: 624 simulated users, 5 rounds. Bayesian assistant final-round accuracy about 81% in Fig 3; random about 37%. Most LLMs show little gain after round 1. Humans (48 users) improved significantly (p=0.002) but stayed below Bayesian. Fine-tuning on Bayesian assistant guesses beat fine-tuning on oracle answers, with about 80% agreement with the Bayesian assistant.
limits: Bar-chart values read from figure text, treat as approximate. Fine-tuning needed, which our no-training agent cannot use. Gemma 2 9B, Llama 3 8B, Qwen 2.5 7B tuned.
agent_relevance: Prompting alone does not give belief updating. Offload the Bayesian update to code or an explicit table the model fills in.

source: Qiu et al. (2025) Bayesian Teaching
finding: Skill learned on one task transferred to hotel and web shopping tasks and to real human users, but verbalized beliefs did not always match behavior.
numbers: Belief-based predictions agree under 50% with direct predictions in some models; for Qwen 2.5, direct accuracy rose after tuning but belief-based accuracy stayed unchanged.
limits: Stated beliefs are not a reliable read of the model working belief.
agent_relevance: Do not trust a model-written probability as the state. Recompute it from logged evidence.

source: Zhao, Lee, Hsu (2023) LLMs as Commonsense Knowledge for Large-Scale Task Planning (LLM-MCTS)
finding: Using the LLM as a world model prior plus policy heuristic inside MCTS beats using it as a policy alone, especially on novel and long tasks.
numbers: VirtualHome success %, seen tasks: GPT3.5-MCTS 91.4 (Simple), 71.2 (Comp), 88.1 (NovelSimple), 72.6 (NovelComp2), 33.6 (NovelComp3) vs GPT3.5 policy 83.4, 47.0, 74.3, 48.2, 5.4. UCT alone 0.0 everywhere. Unseen scenes NovelComp3: 38.8 vs 6.9.
limits: One household simulator, single LLM family at the time. Authors give an MDL argument: a model helps only if it is much shorter than the policy. Table columns read from garbled text; treat as approximate.
agent_relevance: Search over simulated outcomes adds most on hard composite tasks. Gains small on easy ones, so gate by difficulty.

source: Zhao, Lee, Hsu (2023) LLM-MCTS
finding: Boundary case for LLM as world model: it wins where the model is simpler than the policy.
numbers: Multiplication: GPT-4 direct 100% on 1-digit, 99% on 2-digit, 4% on 4-digit; using a 1-digit table plus long multiplication gives 100% at any length.
limits: Argument by analogy; planning is not exactly multiplication.
agent_relevance: Decompose into small verified model calls plus algorithmic control instead of long free-form policies.

source: Hao et al. (2023) Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
finding: Treating reasoning as an MDP with the LLM as world model and MCTS as planner lifts Blocksworld and GSM8K results.
numbers: Blocksworld with LLaMA-33B: RAP(20) 1.00 / 0.88 / 0.42 on 2/4/6-step problems, average 64%, while CoT fails nearly completely; claimed 33% relative gain over GPT-4 CoT. 6-step search space can be as large as 5^6.
limits: Fully observed states; reward is LLM self-evaluation. Compute heavy (10-20 MCTS iterations per step).
agent_relevance: A state-action-reward framing of thinking steps is an MDP. Useful as a control formalism for operators in the schema.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts
finding: Deliberate search over thought states beats chain of thought on tasks needing lookahead.
numbers: Game of 24 with GPT-4: CoT 4% vs ToT 74%.
limits: Many more model calls per task; Game of 24 is fully observable.
agent_relevance: Search buys accuracy at token cost. Pair with a budget rule from the stopping subfields.

source: Lee et al. (2023) Supervised Pretraining Can Learn In-Context RL (DPT)
finding: A transformer trained to predict the optimal action from in-context data behaves like posterior sampling, so it explores without being trained to.
numbers: Online bandits: DPT matches UCB and Thompson sampling in cumulative regret (200 test tasks, robust to unseen noise levels). Theory: regret bound as an implementation of Bayesian posterior sampling.
limits: Needs optimal-action labels and pretraining on a task distribution. DPT trained on a mismatched prior only matches TS; a more representative prior did better.
agent_relevance: Posterior sampling is a cheap exploration rule an agent could imitate in text: sample one hypothesis, act as if true, update.

source: Laskin et al. (2022) In-context Reinforcement Learning with Algorithm Distillation
finding: Sequence model trained on RL learning histories improves in-context across episodes without weight updates, and learns a more data-efficient algorithm than its source.
numbers: Claimed in sparse-reward, combinatorial and pixel tasks; policy distillation baselines do not improve across episodes.
limits: Needs long context across episodes and trained model. Source RL data required. Numbers not extracted this session.
agent_relevance: Cross-attempt memory matters: improvement across tries depends on seeing the history of earlier tries.

source: Shai et al. (2024) Transformers Represent Belief State Geometry in their Residual Stream
finding: Transformers trained on next-token prediction of hidden Markov data linearly encode the optimal belief state, including fractal geometry.
numbers: Mess3 (3 hidden states) belief geometry recovered by linear regression with R2 = 0.95; low similarity to next-token-probability geometry for RRXOR (R2 = 0.31). Belief info spread across layers for RRXOR (36 belief states).
limits: Tiny synthetic HMMs, small transformers; not shown for natural language models.
agent_relevance: Suggests models carry latent beliefs implicitly, so a probe or explicit belief ledger could be read out; unproven for LLM agents.

source: Hu et al. (2025) The Belief State Transformer
finding: Adding a backward token objective forces a compact belief state and fixes goal-conditioned planning that forward-only transformers fail.
numbers: Beats baselines on star-graph navigation (Fig 2). Story writing with known suffix: GPT-4 judge prefers BST 64% of the time, binomial CI [54%, 74%].
limits: Small-scale; authors say it struggles to beat left-to-right in plain language modelling.
agent_relevance: Planning failures may come from missing belief state, not scale. Argues for explicit goal and state notes.

source: Hu et al. (2025) Belief State Transformer
finding: Judge-based evaluation has wide intervals.
numbers: 64% preference with CI [54%, 74%] shows limited evidence.
limits: LLM judge, one judge model.
agent_relevance: Report intervals when comparing scaffold variants with an LLM judge.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Uncertainty of Thoughts (UoT)
finding: Simulating future answer branches and rewarding expected information gain over a possible-state set makes LLMs ask better questions.
numbers: Average success rate gain of 38.1% over direct prompting across 5 datasets and 5 LLMs (20 Questions, medical diagnosis, troubleshooting); Llama3-70B +46.6%. Beats CoT-SC by 33.8%, Reflexion by 29.9%, Original-ToT by 28.3%, Adapted-ToT by 12.4%. DX diagnosis GPT-4 97.0%; MedDG 88.0%; troubleshooting 43.7% -> 67.3%.
limits: Simulation depth limited to three steps for cost. GPT-4 used as answerer; answerer reliability checked on 10% of interactions. Possible-state sets are given. Author list not verified.
agent_relevance: Closest direct test of a belief-state planner for LLM questioning. Supports an information-gain operator under S0 (when to ask).

source: Momennejad et al. (2023) Evaluating Cognitive Maps and Planning in LLMs (CogEval)
finding: Eight LLMs fail at planning on graph structures not in training data: hallucinated edges, overlong paths, loops.
numbers: Shortest path to a state one cluster away on a community graph: GPT-4 success 0 of 30 at temperature 0; never above 10% at temperature 0.5 or 1. Models list edges correctly as (state, action, state) tuples yet fail to use them.
limits: Fully observable graphs, 30 runs per prompt, text prompts.
agent_relevance: Verified state memory is not enough; the model also fails to unroll. Use external search over the graph the model has listed.

source: Papadimitriou, Tsitsiklis (1987) The complexity of Markov decision processes
finding: Finite-horizon POMDP planning is PSPACE-complete; MDPs are P-complete (from memory, not opened).
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Worst-case only; structured instances can be easy.
agent_relevance: Exact belief planning cannot be general. Use approximations and bounded lookahead.

source: Madani, Hanks, Condon (2003) On the undecidability of probabilistic planning
finding: Infinite-horizon undiscounted POMDP policy existence is undecidable (from memory, not opened).
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Applies to undiscounted or goal problems, not discounted ones.
agent_relevance: Always impose a horizon or discount in the agent control loop.

source: Puterman (1994) Markov Decision Processes: Discrete Stochastic Dynamic Programming
finding: Standard reference for MDP theory: value iteration and policy iteration converge to the optimal policy (from memory, not opened).
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Fully observed, known-model assumption.
agent_relevance: Formal ground for treating thinking steps as an MDP when state is observable.

source: Somani, Ye, Hsu, Lee (2013) DESPOT: Online POMDP Planning with Regularization
finding: Plans on a sparse sampled scenario tree with regularization to avoid overfitting to samples (from memory, not opened).
numbers: Not verified this session.
limits: Needs a simulator.
agent_relevance: Regularizing against few sampled hypotheses is a defence against over-trusting a handful of imagined rollouts.
